source.title: Mechanistic Interpretability for Neural TSP Solvers
source.authors: Reuben Narad; Léonard Boussioux; Michael Wagner

record.tranche_reason: The study uses an SAE as an interpretability tool, relying on the superposition/feature-disentangling motivation, but it does not test whether the solver represents more features than dimensions or whether its features overlap.
record.gate_note: The study reports qualitative geometric feature types found with an SAE, recorded below as findings outside the listed claim versions. It does not measure feature overlap, capacity pressure, sparsity-dependent transitions, feature stability or completeness, or whether the model's underlying features are one-dimensional. The cited superposition account is background, not a result of this study. SAE hyperparameter search and reconstruction results are not evidence for the listed claims.
record.test_reason: The study applies a top-k SAE to a TSP solver's encoder residual stream and reports qualitative feature interpretations. Superposition is cited as motivation only. It does not measure feature overlap, capacity, sparsity transitions, neuron polysemanticity, or SAE feature stability or completeness. The system is not an LLM.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors report recurring boundary, cluster and separator features in the encoder via an SAE. They call the work exploratory and correlational, and defer causal, robustness and cross-model tests to future work.
record.recipe_differences: The study applies a top-k SAE to a trained neural TSP solver rather than testing the toy-model superposition setup. It uses one main model and qualitative visual analysis.
record.method_sensitivity: The authors state that feature discoveries may depend on SAE design choices and the underlying policy's training choices; they do not report completed robustness tests showing how these choices change results.

fits_no_version.finding: An SAE on the final encoder residual stream of an RL-trained TSP pointer/Transformer solver yields features that visually look like boundary (convex-hull), cluster-density and separator detectors. Some features are labeled 'Unclear'.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAEs applied to non-language RL-trained combinatorial-optimization models recover human-interpretable geometric features.

record.problems: The feature analysis is qualitative and correlational; the study reports no causal feature interventions, quantitative feature-quality or stability evaluation, or robustness checks. Most analysis is on a single N=100 model trained on a uniform distribution. The authors also state that SAE hyperparameter selection used qualitative interpretability assessment and reconstruction error.
record.rows_left_out: No other claim-relevant result omitted. SAE reconstruction and hyperparameter-search details are autoencoder diagnostics or method-selection information, not tests of the listed claim versions.

untested.parts: No toy model, no feature-count or sparsity sweep, no geometry analysis.
No test of capacity competition or dedicated dimensions for important features.
No test of non-capacity causes of polysemanticity.
Not an LLM. No measure of neuron-level spread or polysemanticity. SAE reconstruction is reported only as 'near-perfect', without numbers.
Stability across seeds, completeness and canonicality are listed as future work, not tested.

record.verdict_notes: The record's links (all 'none') and states are appropriate. Figure 4 also shows an 'Unclear' feature panel, which indicates not all features were interpretable; no quantitative fraction is given. SAE selection used qualitative interpretability judgment, so the reported feature types reflect a curated choice.

versions.untested_parts: No toy-model feature-to-dimension sweep, sparsity-dependent transition, or regular-geometry test.
Does not test polysemanticity as a consequence of limited capacity, or whether important features get dedicated dimensions.
Does not test whether polysemanticity arises through mechanisms other than capacity pressure.
The studied system is a neural TSP solver, not an LLM; the study does not measure feature spread across neurons or test LLM feature recovery.
Qualitative feature interpretations are reported, but completeness, stability, and canonicality of SAE features are not tested.
Does not compare one-dimensional feature directions with multidimensional features or test the dimensionality of the model's underlying features.
